subject: Capacity anchoring & SKU-flex request for Helio expansion
messages:
From: Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@helioanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@helioanalytics.com
Date: 2025-10-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Capacity anchor request for Helio expansion

Thanks Jonas & Karthik —

Following up from our call this morning. Helio is planning a Q1 2026 feature push that will spike inference throughput for our conversational product. We have preliminary forecasts attached (Helio_Q3_forecast.xlsx) showing a 3–4x token increase over the next 12 months.

We want to avoid risky late-stage shortages. Can Redwood provide a short proposal for: 1) a reserved capacity anchor (initial committed GPUs) sized to cover baseline + 30% buffer, and 2) a SKU-flexibility clause that lets us shift between reserved instance classes if pricing/availability changes?

Key constraints: procurement needs a 30–45 day window to review commercial terms. Procurement will need an explicit runbook for swap requests and an approval ladder for discounts above standard thresholds.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

—Lisa
Lisa Chan
Head of Platform, Helio Analytics
Attachment: Helio_Q3_forecast.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@helioanalytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-13T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity anchor request for Helio expansion

Lisa — thanks for the forecast and context. We can definitely propose an anchoring approach that balances your runway and our fleet economics. High level: 

- Proposal: an initial 6-month reserved anchor sized to cover your current baseline + 30% buffer, with an optional ramp schedule linked to verified usage triggers.
- SKU-flex: allow two one-time shifts between reserved SKUs in the first 12 months (e.g., v100 -> a100 variants), subject to 60 days notice and availability; swaps may carry a small reconfiguration fee.
- Pricing sensitivity: we’ll include three discount bands tied to committed token-throughput tiers plus an explicit GPU-cost pass-through clause if market GPU spot prices move >20% sustained for 30 days.

I’m looping in Monica from commercial ops to surface the pricing options and run the math on financial impact. Karthik — can you help draft the conditional swap language and the pass-through guardrails?

If Helio needs tighter protection we can propose a capped escalation clause instead of a full pass-through.

—Jonas
Jonas Weber | Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: —
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-15T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Reserved pricing sensitivity scenarios (internal)

Quick internal note — I ran three scenarios against Helio's forecast and the current GPU market curve. Attached: reserved-pricing-scenarios.csv (summary). Highlights: 

1) Conservative anchor (baseline + 10% buffer): annualized revenue lower but minimal exposure; no discount above 8%.
2) Mid anchor (baseline + 30% buffer): preferred commercial balance — we can offer a 12% discount at 12-month commitment, with an emergency swap allowance (one free swap in year 1, subsequent swaps billed).
3) Aggressive anchor (baseline + 50% buffer): requires executive sign-off; discount band 18–22% with an indexed GPU-cost collar (we absorb up to 10% GPU cost increase, client shares incremental beyond).

Operational notes:
- Swap runbook must include 60-day notice and a rollback clause if capacity not available.
- Finance will need the SOW draft and the HubSpot deal linked to model revenue recognition.

I recommend pushing the mid-anchor by default and offering the indexed collar as an optional add-on if Helio insists on stronger protection.

Attachment: reserved-pricing-scenarios.csv (text/csv)
—Ben
From: Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@helioanalytics.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@helioanalytics.com
Date: 2025-10-17T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity anchor request for Helio expansion

Thanks team — the mid-anchor looks most appealing. A couple of follow ups from procurement: 

- Can you make the swap runbook explicit in the SOW (steps, timelines, who signs approvals)?
- Procurement needs the exact discount matrix and the formula for the GPU-cost collar so our legal can run redlines.
- Timeline: procurement will try to complete review by Nov 20; we need a clean SOW and pricing sheet by Oct 24 to hit that cadence.

Also, is there an alternative to a pure cost pass-through that gives Helio predictability (e.g., a capped pass-through with quarterly reconciliation)? That would be easier for our budgeting.

If you can send a tidy SOW draft + pricing scenarios by EOD Oct 24 we’ll start redlines.

—Lisa
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Chan <lisa.chan@helioanalytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-10-20T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity anchor request for Helio expansion — SOW and limited collar option

Lisa — appreciate the clarity. We can accommodate a capped-collar approach which should be easier for budgeting: 

- Capped collar: Redwood guarantees current pricing up to a 10% GPU cost increase; any increase beyond 10% is passed to the client but capped at a 20% total increase. Quarterly reconciliation will true-up actual spend vs. committed anchor.
- Swap runbook: I attached a short SOW appendix draft that enumerates swap request steps, 60-day windows, approval ladder (manager -> commercial ops -> finance exec), and a rollback trigger if we can’t fulfill swap due to hardware constraints.
- Action items: Jonas to send SOW v1 with pricing matrix & Helio forecast linked; Monica/Ben to confirm revenue recognition and discount approvals required for mid-anchor.

I’m attaching the SOW draft for procurement to kick off redlines. If you’re aligned on the capped-collar we should be able to close commercial terms within the procurement timeline.

Thanks —
Karthik
Sr. Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachment: SOW_draft_Helio_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document)
